tasks.solutionSpace: closure of enumerated residuals within a fixed id set; no new ids, no envelope change
tasks.task:
Close CR13 residuals in r14, no id/envelope changes, blocker if impossible:
1 HIGH retention family filter: the quarantine-name regex admits both families while R5 bounds per family; a snapshot pass can unlink prompts.corrupt-*. Parse <family>.corrupt-..., declare other-family names foreign, and add oracles asserting no cross-family count/unlink plus >=5 seeds per family in AC1-3/AC1-6/AC1-8.
2 HIGH reservation vs fatal create: R3 says any reservation-create failure is fatal, conflicting with AC1-9(b) advance-on-existing-name. Specify fs.ErrExist advances one candidate; any other create error fatal; 4096 exhausted fatal; mirror in AC2-8(b-res).
3 MED R7 vs AC2-6 arm 1: R7's no-record prohibition must scope to records produced by the recovery/retention path, leaving the Durable-loader startup_snapshot_rejected record intact.
4 MED fatal-first/corrupt-second ordering: specify stop-on-first-fatal (snapshot fatal, prompts corrupt => prompts untouched, no record) or accumulate, and add the oracle in AC2-7.
5 MED retention record shape: AC1-6 must assert the full record (warn/startup/failure, error.code=state_directory, kind=resource, retryable=false, canonical remediation) and pin the message literal.
6 MED T2 anchors: quote the snapshot_unavailable/state_directory strings and add read-only anchors wiring.go:486-491 and startup_failure.go:26-33 to T2 inputs.
7 LOW: correct section 9.7 to the actual ticket state (mirror heading says r13; header cites r7; no sha256); pin a numeric FIFO no-block deadline/mechanism (goroutine+select or non-blocking open) and the fixed retention-failure message literal; table-drive all five failure_reason admission cases; add LoadPrompts/SavePrompts never-quarantine negatives to AC1-7; phrase R5 eviction as 'evict while more than four pre-existing remain'; cover the empty-string env value (D4 enables) in AC2-6.
Return the full nine-section spec and a finding-to-text change log.
